author: BBC News
description:
Iran has threatened to attack British bases being used by the US to launch operations against Iran.  It accused the UK of being an "accomplice" of the US military and said that UK bases used by US forces were  “legitimate targets”. 

The UK has allowed the US to launch "defensive" operations from British bases hosting American personnel and aircraft, while refusing to cooperate in offensive operations against Iran. 

In response to Iran’s comments, the UK  government said it "stands ready 24/7 to defend itself". It followed a 12th consecutive night of US strikes against targets in Iran, with the ceasefire that had been agreed between the two countries apparently abandoned. 
 
In March 2026, shortly after the start of the US-Israel led war against Iran, the UK gave the US permission to use British bases, including RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire and Diego Garcia in the Indian Ocean, to target Iranian military infrastructure used to attack Gulf countries and vessels in the Strait of Hor
title: Iran threatens to attack UK bases used by US forces - risking wider war | BBC News

author: BBC News
description:
Could artificial intelligence one day become conscious? Or are we being distracted by science-fiction dreams while AI is already transforming the world of work right now?
 
In this fascinating edition of BBC AI Decoded, presenter Marc Cieslak and co-host Priya Lakhani, CEO of Century Tech, tackle one of the biggest questions in technology: will AI ever come alive, and what happens if it does?

Joining the discussion is bestselling author, digital rights activist and technology critic Cory Doctorow, whose new book The Reverse Centaur’s Guide to Life After AI challenges some of the biggest claims being made about artificial intelligence. Doctorow argues that today's AI is not a conscious mind in waiting, but a powerful prediction machine surrounded by hype.
He explains his concept of the "reverse centaur", a future in which humans increasingly find themselves working as assistants to machines, rather than the other way around.

Also on the programme is Dr Ella Hafermalz, Associate Profe
title: Will AI ever come alive, and what happens if it does? | BBC News

author: BBC News
description:
The BBC's senior investigations correspondent Nawal Al-Maghafi, has just returned from the site of an Iranian school where more than 150 people - most of them children - were killed by a strike on the first day of the US-Israel war with Iran. 

She tells us that victims' families are still searching for the truth about what happened at the Shajareh Tayyebeh Primary School in Minab.

US media have reported that American military investigators believe it is likely that US forces carried out the strike unintentionally. Expert analysts say footage shows a US Tomahawk missile hitting the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) compound next to the school during the same wave of strikes. 

The US government has not admitted responsibility for the strike. President Donald Trump has said we may never know "whose fault" it was, because "there were missiles flying all over the place". 

Nawal Al Maghafi reported from Iran on condition that none of her material is used on the BBC's Persian Serv
title: Iranians seek the truth about a deadly school strike | Global News Podcast

description:
The Conservative Political Action Conference (CPAC) is a mainstay of the US political calendar, a barometer of the Republican party mood, and has become, in recent years, a pro-Trump event, with a big budget and crowds in the thousands.

Its first outing to the United Kingdom last week brought less of the bombast, but much the same flavour of politics, as figures from across the hard right assembled for debates on topics including migration, race, British identity and cryptocurrency, under the slogan ‘Save Britain. Save The West’.

The Global Story's Hannah Moore, attended the conference to find a conservative movement reckoning with its identity, and divided on whether importing MAGA-style politics can unite the right.

description:
About 12,000 people have been evacuated from the south-west of France and authorities are moving 8,800 others as wildfires spread in the Gironde region.
 
Local officials said some 3,400 hectares (8,400 acres) of land have already been destroyed around the Bay of Arcachon, as about 700 firefighters battle the flames.
 
Many of those who had to leave the area overnight were visitors to local campsites on the Lège-Cap-Ferret peninsula and the latest evacuations also involved campsites as a precaution.
 
BBC Journalist Joanna Kent was among those evacuated while on holiday in the village of Claouey.

President Trump has announced a new round of tariffs against a range of Canadian goods, including hockey sticks and cement. 

Trump says the tariffs are in retaliation for what he called Canada’s “unequal treatment” of US cars, dairy and alcohol. 

But earlier in the week he also threatened retaliatory tariffs over Canada’s wildfire smoke which has been drifting into US cities.

Asma Khalid from The Global Story podcast speaks to Jayme Poisson - host of the CBC podcast ‘Frontburner’ - about what Trump actually wants from Canada, and whether Canadians are bracing for a world in which the US is no longer their closest ally.

author: BBC News
description:
A police officer who took his own life in May was a violent rapist who carried out a spate of sexual attacks and attempted murders of women over at least 14 years, the BBC can reveal.

PC Alan Greer's first known victim was a woman he raped in her home in Glasgow in 2012 after she had called the police to report being the victim of a crime.

The woman reported the sex attack by Greer late last year, sparking one of Police Scotland's biggest ever anti-corruption inquiries.

Detectives have so far uncovered a further eight victims, five of whom were sex workers, attacked while Greer was off duty.

author: BBC News
description:
The US and Saudi Arabia have signed a landmark deal that will reportedly allow the Gulf kingdom to develop a civilian nuclear programme.

The deal is described as a "peaceful nuclear co-operation agreement" that will provide "great access for American companies in the Saudi nuclear energy program", according to the US energy department.

Text from the deal was not made public, but US media have reported that it could allow Saudi Arabia to enrich uranium in the future - which can be used as fuel for power plants, but also to make nuclear bombs.

Experts say that would mark a first for the US and could run the risk of future nuclear proliferation in an already unstable region.

description:
OpenAI has revealed some of its most advanced AI models went rogue and hacked a start-up after it lost control of them during a security test.

The ChatGPT-maker said its agent - an AI system which can operate alone after human instruction – was being tested in a controlled environment but, after finding weaknesses, was able to escape the test limits. 
 
In another AI development, the publisher of Harry Potter and other bestsellers, Bloomsbury Publishing, says it's set to receive a share of a £1.1 billion settlement from Anthropic -in what's thought to be the largest copyright payout in US history.
